newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW unveils certificates for overtime pay.
newsitem.headline: VW unveils certificates for overtime pay.

text.p: Germany's Volkswagen AG on Tuesday unveiled a new programme to pay overtime through interest-bearing certificates that can be accumulated and traded in toward early retirement.
VW management board member Peter Hartz said the new programme was in response to changes in German law that will raise retirement ages, putting strain on companies to create new jobs.

VW said its plan, which is available to all 130,000 workers in Germany, would allow workers to retire between 55 and 60. Staff would accumulate certificates instead of cash for overtime hours as well as for work on Saturdays.
"Starting retirement at age 60 is still feasible," Hartz said, noting interest will be paid on the monetary value of the certificates and that they can also be traded within the company.
In order for someone to retire at age 55, Hartz said an employee would need a minimum 1,000 hours worth of the certificates.
Workers between age 55 and 60 typically have an 18-hour workweek at VW, Hartz said.
The new programme is to be discussed with Germany's IG Metall union and would be put into effect for 1997.
